target_audience: University students in Computer Science or Cybersecurity

sections.title: The Privacy Paradox
lecture_lines: Meet Pip and Leo, two users in the forest.
Centralized systems rely on a single 'Forest King' server.
These models track every encounter, risking a surveillance state.
DP-3T replaces central tracking with private, local protection.
This ensures public health without sacrificing individual privacy.
animations: Pip (Penguin) and Leo (Lion) icons appear at LEFT and RIGHT of the screen.
A server icon labeled 'Forest King' (#FF4444) appears in the center.
Pip and Leo move toward each other; lines connect both to the central server.
The server and lines fade out; Pip and Leo are enclosed in green 'Private' circles (#00FF00).
The text 'DP-3T: Privacy-First' appears in the center (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Prerequisite: One-Way Hash Functions
lecture_lines: Cryptographic hashing turns inputs into unique strings.
These one-way functions cannot be reversed.
A secret seed generates unpredictable rolling codes.
animations: A blender icon labeled 'Hash Function' (#FFFFFF) appears in the center.
A yellow 'Seed' block (#FFFF00) enters the blender; green 'Rolling Codes' (#00FF00) flow out.
A red 'One-Way' arrow (#FF0000) appears, indicating the process cannot be reversed.

sections.title: The Daily Secret & Rolling IDs
lecture_lines: Every day, Pip’s phone generates a Secret Day Key.
This key derives a unique code every fifteen minutes.
Frequent rotation prevents tracking by any malicious observer.
animations: Pip's phone icon is shown containing a 'Secret Day Key' (#FFA500).
A code 'A12B' (#00FFFF) pulses from the phone with a '10:00 AM' timestamp.
The code 'A12B' changes to 'C99X' (#00FFFF) with a '10:15 AM' timestamp.

sections.title: The Digital Handshake (Log Storage)
lecture_lines: Nearby phones exchange rolling IDs via Bluetooth.
Observed codes are stored in a local, encrypted diary.
No location data or identities are ever recorded.
animations: Pip and Leo's phones [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] pulse with light blue Bluetooth waves (#ADD8E6) as they pass each other.
Leo's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] displays a folder icon labeled 'Local Diary' (#90EE90).
The code 'A12B' moves from Pip's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] into Leo's 'Local Diary' folder.

sections.title: Sounding the Alarm: The Diagnosis Upload
lecture_lines: If Pip tests positive, he alerts the community anonymously.
He only uploads his daily seeds to a server.
The server broadcasts these keys without any identity data.
Pip's personal information remains safely on his own device.
No contact logs or locations are ever shared externally.
animations: Pip's [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] turns red (#FF0000) and displays a 'Positive Test' icon.
Pip's 'Secret Day Keys' (#FFA500) fly from his [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] to a 'Public Bulletin Board' (#FFFFFF).
The Bulletin Board [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/server.svg] displays the keys with a label 'Anonymous Sick Keys'.
A green 'Privacy Shield' (#00FF00) appears over Pip's identity on his [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg].
The text 'No Personal Data Uploaded' flashes on the screen (#FFFFFF).

sections.title: Local Matching: The Private Detective
lecture_lines: Leo’s phone periodically downloads the latest sick keys.
It uses these keys to recreate potential encounter codes.
The device scans its local diary for any matches.
Finding a match confirms a close encounter with infection.
Leo receives a private exposure alert on his phone.
animations: Leo's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] downloads the 'Secret Day Keys' (#FFA500) from the Public Bulletin Board.
Leo's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] processes the key to recreate the code 'A12B' (#00FFFF).
A magnifying glass (#FFFFFF) scans the 'Local Diary' and finds the matching 'A12B'.
The matching code in the diary flashes yellow (#FFFF00) to indicate a hit.
A red 'Exposure Warning' banner (#FF0000) appears on Leo's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] screen.

sections.title: Summary: Privacy by Design
lecture_lines: DP-3T ensures matching happens only on your device.
The server never learns who met whom.
Cryptography secures health data against surveillance.
animations: A split screen shows a red Centralized web (#FF4444) vs green Decentralized dots (#00FF00).
Lock icons (#FFD700) appear on all phone-to-phone digital handshakes.
The text 'Privacy by Design' scales up and glows in the center (#00FF00).
